answer: Require every agent to bind its identity to a hardware attestation chip: its copper wiring carries a factory-burned pigment signature that software cannot clone. Registration accepts only one active identity per chip and checks a revocation list. To create a thousand fake agents, an attacker must buy a thousand physical chips, pay fabrication and shipping, and risk batch revocation after a single fraud is caught. That linear hardware cost blocks software-only Sybil farms, while honest agents form an oasis of trust because each member is provably scarce.
